facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: audited FY2025 statements and June 30, 2026 interim statements support a reported financial foundation and a last-twelve-months view built from the year and the two six-month periods. - Strongest contrary evidence: the pending take-private merger (10-Q line 273) can change ownership, leverage and the debt structure. The 10-Q lists "risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction" (line 1391). The supplied set does not say how existing debt is treated at closing. - Source risk mechanism: the leases with VICI and GLPI sit in "Long-term financing obligations", not in debt, and their cash cost runs through interest expense (10-K line 1868 "Cash interest paid for rent related to financing obligations"). A consumer that reads only "Total debt" understates fixed obligations. - What cannot proceed: merger financing analysis, covenant headroom on agreement definitions, guarantor-level analysis. - Next evidence action: supply the Merger Agreement (8-K of May 28, 2026, exhibit 2.1, per 10-Q line 305), any merger proxy and financing commitments, the CEI Credit Agreement and indentures, and the VICI and GLPI lease agreements.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The central transaction is a pending take-private. On May 27, 2026, Caesars, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC and its merger subsidiary signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which "Merger Sub will merge with and into the Company, with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation and direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming" (10-Q line 273). The release says the agreement was "announced on May 28, 2026" (release line 106). Each share converts into cash of "$31.00", plus a ticking fee if closing has not occurred by "June 26, 2027" (10-Q line 277). Documentary Fact.

citations.quote: Thesis: Caesars can service its current debt and leases from operations with adequate liquidity, but its lease-adjusted leverage is high, earnings are flat, and a pending change of control with unknown financing is the main credit risk.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. The lease obligations are larger than the debt. Long-term financing obligations of 13,157 exceed total debt of 11,807 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Mechanism: the leases are fixed, rise with inflation, and their cost sits in interest expense, outside Adjusted EBITDA. Implication: lease-adjusted leverage of 5.30x to 6.95x (CP-1 C4, C5), not the debt-only 3.29x, sets leverage tolerance. Analyst Interpretation. 2. A change of control is pending with unknown financing. The Merger Agreement was signed on May 27, 2026 at 31 US dollars per share in cash, subject to stockholder, antitrust and gaming approvals, with an end date that can extend to November 27, 2027 (CP-1A transaction summary). Mechanism: a private owner may add acquisition debt and change the capital structure; the issuer itself lists "increased leverage from the proposed transaction" as a risk (CP-1A Documentary Fact row). Implication: the current credit view may not hold after closing; monitoring posture is event-driven. Documentary Fact for the terms; Insufficient Information for the financing. 3. Coverage is thin on the full basis. Adjusted EBITDA covers total net interest, including lease interest, 1.57x over the last twelve months; after cash rent it covers cash interest on debt 2.87x (CP-1 C6). Mechanism: a fall in Adjusted EBITDA passes almost entirely to coverage because rent and interest are fixed. Implication: limited room for an earnings decline before debt service is strained. Analyst Interpretation. 4. Earnings are flat to slightly down. LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 3,592 is below the FY2025 figure of 3,624, and the margin fell from 31.6% to 30.8% (CP-1 C1, C7); Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was below Q2 2025. Las Vegas declined while Regional grew (CP-1A segment rows). Mechanism: Las Vegas is the largest Adjusted EBITDA segment, so its decline weighs on group cash flow. Implication: deleveraging from earnings growth is not in evidence. Documentary Fact via CP-1 and CP-1A. 5. Liquidity and maturities are not a near-term constraint. Liquidity of 2,928 at June 30, 2026 compares with estimated remaining 2026 debt service of about 425 and lease payments of about 687 (CP-1 liquidity). The first large maturities are the revolver and Term Loan A in 2028 (CP-1 maturity row). Implication: low near-term default risk from liquidity, assuming the capital structure is unchanged. citations.quote: 1. The lease obligations are larger than the debt. Long-term financing obligations of 13,157 exceed total debt of 11,807 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Mechanism: the leases are fixed, rise with inflation, and their cost sits in interest expense, outside Adjusted EBITDA. Implication: lease-adjusted leverage of 5.30x to 6.95x (CP-1 C4, C5), not the debt-only 3.29x, sets leverage tolerance. Analyst Interpretation.

2. A change of control is pending with unknown financing. The Merger Agreement was signed on May 27, 2026 at 31 US dollars per share in cash, subject to stockholder, antitrust and gaming approvals, with an end date that can extend to November 27, 2027 (CP-1A transaction summary). Mechanism: a private owner may add acquisition debt and change the capital structure; the issuer itself lists "increased leverage from the proposed transaction" as a risk (CP-1A Documentary Fact row). Implication: the current credit view may not hold after closing; monitoring posture is event-driven. Documentary Fact for the terms; Insufficient Information for the financing.

3. Coverage is thin on the full basis. Adjusted EBITDA covers total net interest, including lease interest, 1.57x over the last twelve months; after cash rent it covers cash interest on debt 2.87x (CP-1 C6). Mechanism: a fall in Adjusted EBITDA passes almost entirely to coverage because rent and interest are fixed. Implication: limited room for an earnings decline before debt service is strained. Analyst Interpretation.

4. Earnings are flat to slightly down. LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 3,592 is below the FY2025 figure of 3,624, and the margin fell from 31.6% to 30.8% (CP-1 C1, C7); Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was below Q2 2025. Las Vegas declined while Regional grew (CP-1A segment rows). Mechanism: Las Vegas is the largest Adjusted EBITDA segment, so its decline weighs on group cash flow. Implication: deleveraging from earnings growth is not in evidence. Documentary Fact via CP-1 and CP-1A.

5. Liquidity and maturities are not a near-term constraint. Liquidity of 2,928 at June 30, 2026 compares with estimated remaining 2026 debt service of about 425 and lease payments of about 687 (CP-1 liquidity). The first large maturities are the revolver and Term Loan A in 2028 (CP-1 maturity row). Implication: low near-term default risk from liquidity, assuming the capital structure is unchanged. Documentary Fact via CP-1.

6. Debt has been reduced modestly. Total debt face value fell from 11,905 to 11,807, after the 2027 notes were redeemed in July 2025 and share repurchases stopped in 2026 (CP-1, CP-1A governance rows). Implication: the trend is supportive but small relative to the lease-adjusted burden. Documentary Fact.

spans.text: # CP-0 — Source readiness: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (czr)
## Request
- Issuer: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (issuer id `czr`), as of 2026-10-02, information cutoff 2026-10-02 (context).
- Run: `czr-2026-10-02-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`, requested modules CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (the launcher's `minimum` set). CP-0 runs first as their dependency.
- Execution: host session. The host read the pinned files and wrote this answer. No provider was called.
- Question: can the supplied public filings support CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and what remains blocked?
- Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. No credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion; no figures normalized, reconciled or calculated.
## Sources
| Source | sha256 | Role |
| CZR_FY2025_10K.txt | 172309048af2a6a2dab515d765f00a7c89bf8c874c6104a5e3a052b66cad4512 | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 (text, 3,401 lines) |
| CZR_Q2_2026_10Q.txt | f369ce5f1ebeddd9a0d4ce02ce3958112267d8701d1a348dfd6dc82d2034793a | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (text, 1,557 lines) |
| CZR_Q2_2026_Earnings_Release.txt | b385f76ff631243d1053fa8073ebde4f8886b4a50c9ce34ce3498d6b2ac3e9f8 | Exhibit 99.1 earnings release dated July 28, 2026 (text, 194 lines) |
| context | 70a1a94c5cc4a6bf8f11bf47e9f0a41d9be046e2bcfa93425809b6450d15d5c1 | User run settings; not issuer evidence |
Supplied handoffs: none (CP-0 is the first module). Locators are line numbers of the pinned text files.
## Findings
### Readiness verdict
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 statements and unaudited June 30, 2026 interim statements with comparatives are located. Text conversion flattens tables; no original HTML or XBRL is supplied. |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business, segments, history, the pending merger and debt descriptions are located. The Merger Agreement, debt documents, leases and proxy statement are not supplied. |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | CP-2 can synthesise from CP-1 and CP-1A and the located covenant, lease and liquidity text. Merger financing terms and the post-closing capital structure are not supplied. |
| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | All sources are text with stable line numbers, so claims can be traced. Visual and table-layout checks against the filed HTML are not possible. |
Command sheet: CP-1 RUN; CP-1A RUN; CP-2 RUN; CP-5 RUN.
### Source register
#### Form 10-K for FY2025 (`CZR_FY2025_10K.txt`)

- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for the audited consolidated statements. Line 1 onward: "FORM 10-K", "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025", "Commission File No. 001-36629 CAESARS ENTERTAINMENT, INC.".
- Audit: line 1625 "REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM"; line 1676 "We have served as the Company’s auditor since 2020." Signature date: line 3396 "February 17, 2026".

- Statements located: balance sheet from line 1680, statements of operations from line 1726, cash flows from line 1811. Debt note from line 2344 ("Note 9. Long-Term Debt"). Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation from line 1318, marked unaudited. Liquidity table at line 1353.
- Units: line 1682 "(Dollars in millions, except par value)"; line 1728 "(In millions, except per share data)". USD.

- Perimeter: consolidated Caesars Entertainment, Inc. with noncontrolling interests (line 1755 "Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests"). Line 1343: "We are a holding company, and our only significant assets are ownership interests in our subsidiaries."
#### Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (`CZR_Q2_2026_10Q.txt`)
- Family and authority: filed quarterly report with unaudited condensed statements. Line 1 onward: "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026". Signature: line 1552 "Date: July 28, 2026".

- Statements: balance sheet from line 64 (June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025), statements of operations from line 104 (three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025), cash flows from line 197 (six months). Debt note from line 490. Covenant text from line 587. Merger note from line 272. Liquidity from line 1273.
- Units: line 66 "(In millions)". USD.
#### Earnings release (`CZR_Q2_2026_Earnings_Release.txt`)

- Family and authority: issuer press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1, dated "(July 28, 2026)" (line 3). Management-prepared, unaudited. It repeats the 10-Q statement of operations (lines 142 to 178) and adds segment Adjusted EBITDA (lines 52 to 67), net debt (lines 70 to 80) and an Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (lines 179 to 191).

- It states facts that are not in the 10-Q tables: "Net debt (a) | $10,842 | $11,018" (line 78) and a debt split by "Bank debt and loans" and "Notes" (lines 74 to 75). These are issuer non-GAAP presentations.
- Version relationship: its statement of operations duplicates the 10-Q. Treat the 10-Q as controlling for statement facts. Do not count the release as independent corroboration of them.
### Information-availability boundary
- All three documents are dated before the as-of date and the cutoff: the 10-K on February 17, 2026, and the 10-Q and release on July 28, 2026.
- Nothing dated between July 28, 2026 and the as-of date is supplied. Events in that window, for example the merger vote, regulatory approvals or merger financing, are Not supplied, not absent.
### Identity and perimeter
- Reporting entity: Caesars Entertainment, Inc., Delaware, NASDAQ "CZR" (10-K lines 1 to 92).
- Debt issuer and borrower: "CEI" credit facilities and notes (10-Q lines 494 to 505); Caesars Virginia facilities ("CVA") are a separate borrower group with their own covenants (10-Q line 599).
- Lease counterparties: VICI and GLPI; the leases are accounted for as financing obligations (10-K line 1705 "Long-term financing obligations"; release line 96).

- Pending owner: Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC under the Merger Agreement signed May 27, 2026 (10-Q line 273). The release says the agreement was "announced on May 28, 2026" (line 106). Signing and announcement are different events, not a conflict.
- Unresolved: guarantor and restricted-group detail is not in the supplied text; the context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank, which is not evidence of their absence.
### Consumer evidence demand
| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, debt, liquidity, non-GAAP | 10-K lines 1680 to 1860, 2344 to 2370; 10-Q lines 64 to 250, 490 to 520; release lines 9 to 191 | Text conversion; financing obligations are a large liability class separate from debt |

| CP-1A | Business, segments, history, transaction, ownership | 10-K lines 88 to 100; 10-Q lines 272 to 305; release lines 9 to 70 | Merger Agreement, merger proxy and 2026 proxy statement not supplied |
| CP-2 | CP-1 and CP-1A outputs; covenants; lease burden; liquidity | 10-Q lines 587 to 600 and 1273 to 1300 | Executed agreements not supplied; covenant definitions not verifiable |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims | All three sources have line numbers | Original HTML and XBRL not supplied |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: audited FY2025 statements and June 30, 2026 interim statements support a reported financial foundation and a last-twelve-months view built from the year and the two six-month periods.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the pending take-private merger (10-Q line 273) can change ownership, leverage and the debt structure. The 10-Q lists "risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction" (line 1391). The supplied set does not say how existing debt is treated at closing.

- Source risk mechanism: the leases with VICI and GLPI sit in "Long-term financing obligations", not in debt, and their cash cost runs through interest expense (10-K line 1868 "Cash interest paid for rent related to financing obligations"). A consumer that reads only "Total debt" understates fixed obligations.
- What cannot proceed: merger financing analysis, covenant headroom on agreement definitions, guarantor-level analysis.

- Next evidence action: supply the Merger Agreement (8-K of May 28, 2026, exhibit 2.1, per 10-Q line 305), any merger proxy and financing commitments, the CEI Credit Agreement and indentures, and the VICI and GLPI lease agreements.
## Calculations
No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |
| Merger Agreement, merger financing and post-closing capital structure not supplied | High | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the 8-K exhibit 2.1 and any merger proxy or financing documents |
| Events between July 28, 2026 and the as-of date not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply later 8-Ks or confirm none |

Implication: Caesars should be read as a highly levered, lease-heavy credit; the debt-only ratio overstates its flexibility.

- Coverage: Adjusted EBITDA covers total net interest, which includes lease interest, only 1.57x. After cash rent, Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest on debt 2.87x. Interest coverage is thin on the full basis and improving slowly as debt falls.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The central transaction is a pending take-private. On May 27, 2026, Caesars, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC and its merger subsidiary signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which "Merger Sub will merge with and into the Company, with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation and direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming" (10-Q line 273). The release says the agreement was "announced on May 28, 2026" (release line 106). Each share converts into cash of "$31.00", plus a ticking fee if closing has not occurred by "June 26, 2027" (10-Q line 277). Documentary Fact.

Conditions and protection. Closing needs approval "by the holders of at least a majority of all of the outstanding shares", expiry of the HSR Act waiting period and "certain gaming regulatory approvals" (10-Q line 294). Either party may terminate if the merger has not closed by May 27, 2027, with automatic extensions to August 27, 2027 and November 27, 2027 while only regulatory conditions remain (10-Q line 296). Caesars would owe "a termination fee of $200 million" in specified circumstances; Fertitta Gaming would owe "a reverse termination fee of $450 million" if the merger fails on antitrust or gaming-law grounds or at the end date with only regulatory conditions open (10-Q lines 297 to 298). A no-shop applies from "July 11, 2026" (10-Q line 290). Documentary Fact.

Financing and existing debt. The supplied documents do not describe how Fertitta Gaming will fund the merger or how the existing CEI credit facilities, notes and VICI and GLPI leases are treated at closing. The 10-Q lists among its risks "the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all" and "risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction" (10-Q line 1391). The Merger Agreement is exhibit 2.1 to the 8-K of May 28, 2026 (10-Q line 305), which is not in the source set. Insufficient Information.

Recent debt activity. On July 8, 2025, Caesars "fully redeemed all of the $546 million outstanding principal amount of the CEI Senior Notes due 2027", funded by revolver borrowings and proceeds of a note receivable from the WSOP trademark sale (10-K line 1367). No new bond issue is described for 2026 in the supplied documents; the six-month cash flows show revolver and term-loan borrowings and repayments (CP-1 cash-flow table). Earlier divestitures raised cash: the WSOP trademark for "$500 million" on October 29, 2024, and The LINQ Promenade for "$275 million" on December 12, 2024 (10-K lines 1053 to 1054). Documentary Fact.

Liquidity effect, as Analyst Interpretation: before closing, liquidity of about 2.9 billion (CP-1) covers the remaining 2026 debt service and lease payments the issuer estimates. After closing, liquidity and leverage depend on the acquisition financing, which is Not supplied.

## Request
- Issuer: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (issuer id `czr`), as of 2026-10-02, information cutoff 2026-10-02.
- Run: `czr-2026-10-02-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`. Fills "Key findings" and "Strengths and weaknesses".
- Execution: host session. This synthesis uses the supplied handoffs only; it quotes no source text. No provider was called.
- Reader question: what is the fundamental credit view, and which strengths, weaknesses, findings and risks drive it? No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
Issuer sources pinned for this run (read by upstream modules, not quoted here):
| Source | sha256 |
| CZR_Q2_2026_Earnings_Release.txt | b385f76ff631243d1053fa8073ebde4f8886b4a50c9ce34ce3498d6b2ac3e9f8 |
Supplied handoffs consumed:
| Module | sha256 | Used for |

| CP-0 | c25e5a54d628dec4614d6d52f99b207b6b261bfcb442c3bed0d41c0af7f514a3 | Readiness and restrictions: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for CP-2; no merger financing, executed agreements or post-July 28, 2026 events |

| CP-1 | 61c83d3e3ee8df68a362930def996cf678e2e35924dc16aa46093cfd4d02ba30 | All figures: LTM and FY2025 metrics, leverage on three bases (C3 to C5), coverage (C6), free cash flow (C2), debt register, liquidity, covenant terms |
| CP-1A | 89de62ee6354c11acba13cac4ef871638c52f2ac6bcb8731ef91f99f58e5c17f | Business rows, merger terms, governance behaviour, timeline, credit translations |
Upstream status: all three accepted. Inherited limitations: CP-1A rates merger financing and debt treatment Insufficient Information; CP-1 rates covenant headroom Not calculable.
## Findings
### Credit assessment

Caesars is a large, diversified gaming operator whose credit profile is set by heavy fixed obligations: about 11.8 billion of debt and about 13.2 billion of lease financing obligations to VICI and GLPI (CP-1 debt and lease rows). Debt-only leverage of 3.29x (CP-1 C3) understates the burden; with the leases, leverage is 6.95x on carrying amounts (CP-1 C4) or 5.30x on debt over Adjusted EBITDA after cash rent (CP-1 C5), and Adjusted EBITDA covers total net interest only 1.57x (CP-1 C6). Near-term liquidity is adequate: about 2.9 billion of cash and revolver capacity, no large maturity before 2028, and free cash flow of about 0.6 billion over the last twelve months (CP-1 liquidity table, C2). The dominant open question is the pending take-private by Fertitta Gaming: the supplied documents do not show its financing or how existing debt and leases are treated, so the post-closing credit profile cannot be assessed (CP-1A transaction summary).
- Category: Analyst Interpretation, based on CP-1 figures and CP-1A Documentary Fact rows.
- Confidence: Medium. Reported figures are complete and reconcile; the merger financing is missing, which limits any view beyond the current capital structure.

Thesis: Caesars can service its current debt and leases from operations with adequate liquidity, but its lease-adjusted leverage is high, earnings are flat, and a pending change of control with unknown financing is the main credit risk.
### Key findings

1. The lease obligations are larger than the debt. Long-term financing obligations of 13,157 exceed total debt of 11,807 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Mechanism: the leases are fixed, rise with inflation, and their cost sits in interest expense, outside Adjusted EBITDA. Implication: lease-adjusted leverage of 5.30x to 6.95x (CP-1 C4, C5), not the debt-only 3.29x, sets leverage tolerance. Analyst Interpretation.

2. A change of control is pending with unknown financing. The Merger Agreement was signed on May 27, 2026 at 31 US dollars per share in cash, subject to stockholder, antitrust and gaming approvals, with an end date that can extend to November 27, 2027 (CP-1A transaction summary). Mechanism: a private owner may add acquisition debt and change the capital structure; the issuer itself lists "increased leverage from the proposed transaction" as a risk (CP-1A Documentary Fact row). Implication: the current credit view may not hold after closing; monitoring posture is event-driven. Documentary Fact for the terms; Insufficient Information for the financing.

3. Coverage is thin on the full basis. Adjusted EBITDA covers total net interest, including lease interest, 1.57x over the last twelve months; after cash rent it covers cash interest on debt 2.87x (CP-1 C6). Mechanism: a fall in Adjusted EBITDA passes almost entirely to coverage because rent and interest are fixed. Implication: limited room for an earnings decline before debt service is strained. Analyst Interpretation.

4. Earnings are flat to slightly down. LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 3,592 is below the FY2025 figure of 3,624, and the margin fell from 31.6% to 30.8% (CP-1 C1, C7); Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was below Q2 2025. Las Vegas declined while Regional grew (CP-1A segment rows). Mechanism: Las Vegas is the largest Adjusted EBITDA segment, so its decline weighs on group cash flow. Implication: deleveraging from earnings growth is not in evidence. Documentary Fact via CP-1 and CP-1A.

5. Liquidity and maturities are not a near-term constraint. Liquidity of 2,928 at June 30, 2026 compares with estimated remaining 2026 debt service of about 425 and lease payments of about 687 (CP-1 liquidity). The first large maturities are the revolver and Term Loan A in 2028 (CP-1 maturity row). Implication: low near-term default risk from liquidity, assuming the capital structure is unchanged. Documentary Fact via CP-1.

6. Debt has been reduced modestly. Total debt face value fell from 11,905 to 11,807, after the 2027 notes were redeemed in July 2025 and share repurchases stopped in 2026 (CP-1, CP-1A governance rows). Implication: the trend is supportive but small relative to the lease-adjusted burden. Documentary Fact.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths:

- Scale and diversification: 52 properties in 18 states and a digital business in 34 jurisdictions spread revenue across markets (CP-1A business rows). This supports revenue visibility. Documentary Fact.
- Cash generation: LTM operating cash flow of 1,297 and free cash flow of 610 after capex (CP-1 C1, C2). Free cash flow is positive and rising as capex falls. Documentary Fact via CP-1.
- Liquidity runway: 2,928 of liquidity and no large maturity before 2028 (CP-1). Documentary Fact via CP-1.
- Reported covenant compliance: the issuer states compliance with all applicable financial covenants at June 30, 2026 (CP-1 covenant table). Management Language; headroom is not verifiable.
Weaknesses:
- Lease-heavy capital structure: financing obligations exceed debt, and rent is inflation-linked (CP-1 lease rows). Lease-adjusted leverage is high. Analyst Interpretation.
- Thin interest coverage: 1.57x on total net interest (CP-1 C6). Analyst Interpretation.
- Flat earnings and a falling Las Vegas segment (CP-1 C1; CP-1A segment rows). Documentary Fact.
- Persistent GAAP net losses since FY2024, because interest including lease interest exceeds operating income (CP-1 income statement). Documentary Fact.

- Ownership uncertainty: a pending take-private with unknown financing (CP-1A transaction summary). Insufficient Information on financing; the missing datapoint is the post-closing debt and lease structure.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Leveraged take-private | New owner funds the purchase with debt or changes the structure; existing creditors' ranking and covenants may change | Higher leverage and default risk after closing; possible change-of-control effects, terms Not supplied | Critical |
| Lease burden | Fixed, CPI-linked rent to VICI and GLPI absorbs a large part of Adjusted EBITDA | Lower leverage tolerance; less cash for debt service in a downturn | Material |
| Earnings decline in Las Vegas | Largest Adjusted EBITDA segment is falling | Coverage weakens because fixed charges do not fall | Material |
| Consumer spending cycle | Gaming and hospitality demand is discretionary | Earnings and coverage fall together in a recession | Material |
| Covenant definitions unknown | Net leverage and fixed-charge covenants of 6.50:1 and 2.0:1 apply to the revolver and Term Loan A; definitions not supplied | Headroom cannot be monitored | Minor |
### Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Merger financing and treatment of existing debt and leases | The post-closing credit profile is unknown | Assessment confidence, key finding 2, top risk | Critical | Supply the Merger Agreement and financing documents; rerun CP-2 when filed |
| Events after July 28, 2026 | Approval and financing status at the as-of date unknown | Monitoring posture | Material | Supply later filings |

| Executed credit agreement, indentures and leases | Covenant headroom, change-of-control and restricted-payment terms unknown | Covenant risk, governance capacity | Material | Supply documents and add CP-4 |
| No rating or market data | No external view of the credit | Not required for this scope | Minor | Add CP-2H or CP-3D only if sourced |
## Calculations
No new calculation. Every figure refers to a CP-1 row or calculation ID (C1 to C12).
## Gaps
- Critical: merger financing and post-closing structure Not supplied.
- Material: events after July 28, 2026 Not supplied; executed agreements Not supplied.
- Minor: no rating or market data in scope.
## Next module
- CP-5: trace each finding to its CP-1 row or calculation and its CP-1A row, and check that categories match the basis.
- Report delivery: "Key findings" and "Strengths and weaknesses" above; carry the Medium confidence and the Critical merger gap.
